facts.text: A light-year measures the distance light travels in one year, approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres.
Light travels through space at approximately 300,000 kilometres per second. Large distances therefore still take time to cross.
Earth is approximately eight light-minutes from the Sun.
From these definitions, light from a hypothetical object five light-years away takes five years to arrive. This is a worked implication of the distance definition, not a claim about a named object.

facts.text: A set is an unordered collection without duplicate elements; it supports membership tests and operations such as intersection and union. Do not promise a set's iteration order.
A dictionary maps unique keys to values. Assigning a value to an existing key replaces that key's previous value. Dictionary iteration preserves insertion order.
Accessing an absent dictionary key with subscripting raises KeyError. dict.get can instead return None or an explicitly supplied default.
Lists are ordered sequences and may contain repeated elements. Code may use an explicit loop, membership test and append to keep first occurrences in their original order.

facts.text: CORS uses HTTP response headers to tell browsers which other origins may read a response. Origin includes scheme, host and port.

Some cross-origin browser requests first send an OPTIONS preflight describing the planned method and headers. A preflight checks permission; it is not the actual application request. Not every cross-origin request needs a preflight.

Browser fetch and XMLHttpRequest enforce the same-origin policy unless the response has appropriate CORS headers. CORS concerns browser access to responses, not a general guarantee that the server did or did not process a request.
JavaScript receives limited details of a CORS failure; the browser console provides more information. Diagnosing a specific request requires its actual error and request/response details.
